findings.where: First screen (hero), at desktop and phone, and the whole tile
findings.fault: Mark is never seen. The first screen is the aqueduct mark, his name in carved capitals, one line of text and the button. No photo of him appears anywhere in the tile, and no slot shows where a portrait or video of him would sit in this stone look. The only image slot is the ashlar texture. So the tile does not show how 'the man himself' would look in this direction.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff choosing one advisor want to see the real, named person before they write. Mark and the founder would object too: client value 3 asks every tile to answer 'Mark is seen and heard', and first-visit trust item 1 always applies to a solo practice. Without that slot, the direction can't be judged on what matters most for trust.

findings.where: Hero heading: 'MARK · M · MOSELEY' in red Roman capitals on grey stone, under the aqueduct mark
findings.fault: A person's full name, split by interpuncts and painted red on dressed grey stone under an arch, reads like a memorial or a dedication tablet, not like a living advisor you can write to today. The monument treatment also makes him remote and institutional where the brief asks for approachable.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor from a development agency, who may get a funereal or self-monumentalising first impression of a solo consultant. Mark would also object, since §5 asks for a personal, approachable voice and value 6 asks for confidence without grandeur.

findings.where: Hero button 'WRITE TO MARK' and nav 'CONTACT'
findings.fault: The only way to get in touch is a mailto: link whose address is never shown. A visitor who uses webmail or has no mail app set up clicks it and nothing useful happens. They can't copy the address either, because it appears nowhere on the page.
findings.who_objects: Agency staff on locked-down work machines or webmail, who often have no default mail client, would hit a dead end at the one action the page exists for. First-visit trust item 7 asks for the email address in full as its own link text.

findings.where: Article page specimen: the line under the headline, 'MMM INFRA BLOG NO. 8 · 18 SEPTEMBER 2024'
findings.fault: The article page names the firm but not the author. There is no 'Mark Moseley' and no one-line bio, so a reader who arrives from a LinkedIn post can't see whose judgement they are reading.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader landing on an article from a shared link: the article is the proof of judgement, and it only works as proof if it is tied to the named person (first-visit trust item 12).
